title: Library Closing Early
text: The Main Library will close at 6 p.m. this Friday instead of 10 p.m. because of a staff meeting. The study rooms on the second floor will also be locked. Students can use the Science Building reading room until 9 p.m. Normal hours start again on Saturday at 9 a.m.

stem: What is the main purpose of the notice?
options: To explain how to book a study room
To advertise a new reading room
explanation: The notice says the library 'will close at 6 p.m. this Friday instead of 10 p.m.', so its purpose is to announce an early closing. The study rooms are mentioned only as a detail, and no volunteers are requested.

stem: Where can students study on Friday until 9 p.m.?
explanation: The text says students 'can use the Science Building reading room until 9 p.m.' The Main Library and its study rooms are closed by then.

title: Study Group Delay
text:
Priya (3:10): Are you coming to the study group today?
Marcus (3:12): Yes, but I'll be 15 minutes late. My bus is stuck in traffic.
Priya (3:13): No problem. We're in Room 204.
Marcus (3:14): Can you save me a seat? I'm bringing the notes.
Priya (3:15): Sure. See you soon!

stem: Why will Marcus be late?
explanation: Marcus writes, 'My bus is stuck in traffic.' This means the bus is delayed. He is bringing the notes, so he did not forget them.

stem: What does Marcus ask Priya to do?
options: Meet him at the bus stop
explanation: Marcus asks, 'Can you save me a seat?' Saving a seat means keeping a place for him. He is the one bringing the notes, so Priya does not need to send them.

title: Campus Cafe Lunch
text:
Campus Cafe Lunch Special (11 a.m. to 2 p.m.)
Soup of the day with bread: $4
Chicken sandwich with salad: $7
Vegetable pasta: $6
All lunch specials include a free small drink. Students get 10% off with a valid ID. We do not accept cash. Please pay by card.

stem: What is true about the lunch specials?
explanation: The menu says 'All lunch specials include a free small drink.' Only the pasta is described as vegetable, and students get a discount but anyone can order.

stem: How can a customer pay?
explanation: The menu says 'We do not accept cash. Please pay by card.' A student ID gives a discount but is not a way to pay.

title: Visitor Parking Lot B
text:
VISITOR PARKING: LOT B
Maximum stay: 2 hours. Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
Visitors must show a ticket from the machine. After 5 p.m., permit holders only.
Cars without a valid ticket or permit may be towed.

stem: Who can park in Lot B at 7 p.m.?
explanation: The sign says 'After 5 p.m., permit holders only.' The two-hour visitor rule applies during the day, from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

stem: What may happen to a car with no ticket or permit?
options: The driver must pay at the gate
The owner will get a free pass
It must leave after two hours
explanation: The sign warns that such cars 'may be towed,' which means a truck may take them away. The two-hour limit is for visitors who have a ticket.

title: Roommate Meeting
text:
Subject: Roommate meeting
Hi everyone, let's meet on Sunday at 4 p.m. in the kitchen to talk about the cleaning schedule. Some of us have been forgetting to take out the trash. Please bring your class timetables so we can plan fairly. I'll bring snacks. Aisha

stem: Why is Aisha writing the email?
options: To ask for help with homework
To call a meeting on chores
explanation: Aisha invites everyone to 'talk about the cleaning schedule,' so she wants a meeting about chores. The trash is mentioned as the reason, not as a complaint about noise.

stem: What should the roommates bring?
explanation: Aisha asks them to 'bring your class timetables,' which are class schedules. She says she will bring the snacks herself.

title: Campus Shuttle Times
text:
Campus Shuttle: Weekdays
Departs North Gate: 7:30, 8:00, 8:30, 9:00
Departs Library: 7:45, 8:15, 8:45, 9:15
No shuttle on weekends or holidays.
The last shuttle of the day leaves the library at 9:15 p.m.

stem: When does the second morning shuttle leave North Gate?
explanation: The North Gate times are 7:30, 8:00, 8:30 and 9:00, so the second one leaves at 8:00. The times 7:45 and 8:15 belong to the library.

stem: What does the timetable say about weekends?
options: The shuttle only goes to the library
explanation: The timetable says 'No shuttle on weekends or holidays,' so the shuttle does not run. It does not mention fewer trips or a later start.

title: Photo Club Meeting
text: Photo Club news! Our first meeting of the semester is Thursday at 5 p.m. in Art Room 3. New members are welcome, and you do not need a fancy camera. A phone is fine! We will go on a short walk around campus to take pictures. Bring a jacket because it may be cold.

stem: What will the club do at the first meeting?
explanation: The post says 'We will go on a short walk around campus to take pictures.' This means taking pictures outside. A fancy camera is not needed, so buying cameras is not part of the plan.

stem: What does the post say about cameras?
options: Members must bring a good one
explanation: The post says 'you do not need a fancy camera. A phone is fine!' This means a phone camera is enough. It does not say the club lends cameras.

title: Bookstore Receipt
text:
University Bookstore
Biology textbook: $48.00
Notebook (2): $6.00
Pen set: $3.50
Total: $57.50
Paid by card
Returns accepted within 14 days with this receipt. Books must not be written in.

stem: What is the total cost?
explanation: The total printed on the receipt is $57.50. The textbook and notebooks together cost $54.00, but the pen set adds $3.50.

stem: What does the customer need to return an item?
explanation: The receipt says returns are accepted 'within 14 days with this receipt.' It does not ask for a student card or a box.

title: Laundry Room Alert
text: Laundry Alert: Your wash in Machine 6 is finished. Please collect your clothes within 15 minutes so others can use the machine. After that, staff may move your clothes to the shelf. Tap here to book your next wash.

stem: What is the main purpose of the message?
options: To tell the user their laundry is ready
To explain how to wash clothes
To ask the user to pay
explanation: The message begins 'Your wash in Machine 6 is finished,' so it tells the user the laundry is ready. It does not ask for payment or give washing instructions.

stem: What might happen after 15 minutes?
options: The clothes may be moved to a shelf
The user will have to pay more
explanation: The message says 'staff may move your clothes to the shelf.' It says nothing about extra payment or locking the room.

title: Dinner Plans
text:
Sofia (6:02): I'm at the store. Do we need milk or just bread?
Hamza (6:05): We need both. And eggs, please.
Sofia (6:06): OK. I'll get them. Do you want pasta tonight?
Hamza (6:08): Yes! I'll cook. I'm already home.
Sofia (6:09): Great. Be there in 20 minutes.

stem: What does Hamza ask Sofia to buy?
explanation: Hamza says 'We need both. And eggs, please.' Both refers to milk and bread, so he wants milk, bread and eggs. He is cooking the pasta, so it is not on the shopping list.

stem: What will Hamza do next?
explanation: Hamza says 'I'll cook. I'm already home.' Sofia is the one still at the store, and she will arrive in 20 minutes.

title: Gym Pool Closed
text: The pool at the Student Gym is closed for cleaning from Monday, March 3, to Wednesday, March 5. It will reopen on Thursday at 6 a.m. The gym, running track and weight room will stay open as usual. Members can ask the front desk for a free day pass to the city pool.

stem: When will the pool open again?
explanation: The notice says the pool 'will reopen on Thursday at 6 a.m.' Wednesday, March 5, is the last day it is closed.

stem: What can members do while the pool is closed?
options: Use a free pass at another pool
explanation: Members 'can ask the front desk for a free day pass to the city pool.' The notice does not mention refunds, and the gym itself stays open.

title: Free Math Tutoring
text:
FREE MATH TUTORING
Stuck on homework? Student tutors can help with Algebra 1 and 2 and Statistics.
Mondays and Wednesdays, 4 to 6 p.m., Learning Center, Room 12.
No appointment needed. Just bring your book and your questions.

stem: Who can get help from the tutors?
options: Any student who needs math help
explanation: The flyer offers help with Algebra 1 and 2 and Statistics, and says 'No appointment needed.' So any student who needs help in these areas can come.

stem: What should students bring?
explanation: The flyer ends 'Just bring your book and your questions.' The service is free, so no payment is needed.

title: Late Assignment
text:
Subject: Assignment 3
Dear Ms. Rivera, I am sorry that my assignment is late. I was sick with the flu for three days last week. I have finished the work and attached it to this email. Could I please have until Friday to submit it? Thank you for your understanding. Chen Li

stem: Why is Chen writing to Ms. Rivera?
options: To ask a question about the flu
To report a problem with the homework
To thank her for a good grade
To explain a delay and ask for more time
explanation: Chen apologizes for the late assignment and asks 'Could I please have until Friday to submit it?' So he is explaining a delay and asking for extra time. He does not ask about the flu itself.

stem: Why was the assignment late?
options: Chen was away on a trip
explanation: Chen says 'I was sick with the flu for three days last week.' Being sick is the reason given, and no other reason is mentioned.

title: Chemistry Lab Rules
text:
CHEMISTRY LAB: SAFETY RULES
1. Wear goggles and a lab coat at all times.
2. No food or drinks.
3. Long hair must be tied back.
4. Tell the instructor at once if something spills.

stem: What must students do with long hair?
explanation: Rule 3 says 'Long hair must be tied back.' The sign does not mention hats or washing.

stem: What should a student do after a spill?
options: Clean it with a paper towel
explanation: Rule 4 says to 'Tell the instructor at once if something spills.' The sign does not tell students to clean it up themselves.

title: Borrowing a Charger
text:
Amara (9:40): Hi Lucas, do you have a phone charger I can borrow? Mine broke this morning.
Lucas (9:42): I have one in my bag. I'm in the library, second floor.
Amara (9:43): Thanks! I have a class at 10:00. Can I come now?
Lucas (9:44): Sure. I'll wait by the stairs.
Amara (9:45): Perfect. Two minutes!

stem: Why does Amara message Lucas?
options: She wants to borrow a charger
She needs a ride to class
explanation: Amara asks, 'do you have a phone charger I can borrow? Mine broke this morning.' The charger is broken, not the phone, and nothing is stolen.

stem: Where will Amara meet Lucas?
options: Near the stairs in the library
explanation: Lucas is 'in the library, second floor' and says 'I'll wait by the stairs.' Amara's class is at 10:00, but they are not meeting there.

title: Water Shut-off
text: Notice to residents of Oak Hall: The water will be turned off on Tuesday from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. while workers repair a pipe. Please fill a bottle with water before 9 a.m. if you need it. The bathrooms will be closed during this time. Use the ones in the Student Center.

stem: What is the main purpose of the notice?
options: To ask residents to pay a bill
To explain a rule about bottles
To tell residents about a repair
To invite residents to a party
explanation: The notice says the water 'will be turned off' while workers 'repair a pipe,' so it informs residents of a repair. Bottles are only a suggestion.

stem: Where should residents go to use a bathroom on Tuesday morning?
explanation: The notice says 'Use the ones in the Student Center.' The Oak Hall bathrooms are closed from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.

title: Bus Delay Alert
text: Bus Alert: Route 5 to Downtown is running about 12 minutes late because of road work on Elm Street. The next bus will arrive at Main Stop at 8:27 a.m. instead of 8:15 a.m. Route 9 is running on time. We are sorry for the delay.

stem: Why is Route 5 late?
explanation: The alert says Route 5 is late 'because of road work on Elm Street.' It does not mention the driver, the bus or weather.

stem: What can a rider infer from the alert?
options: The next Route 5 bus comes at 8:27
Elm Street is closed all day
explanation: Route 5 will arrive 'at 8:27 a.m. instead of 8:15 a.m.' Route 9 'is running on time,' and the bus is late, not cancelled.

title: Lost Backpack
text: Lost: a blue backpack with a small yellow tag. I left it on a bench near the Science Building on Monday around 3 p.m. It has my laptop and my notebooks inside. If you find it, please message me or take it to the Security Office. I will give a reward. Please help! Yuki

stem: What does Yuki want people to do?
options: Contact her if they find it
explanation: Yuki writes 'If you find it, please message me or take it to the Security Office.' So she wants people to contact her or return the bag. The bench is only where she lost it.

stem: What is inside the backpack?
options: A yellow tag and a jacket
explanation: Yuki says 'It has my laptop and my notebooks inside.' The yellow tag is on the outside of the bag, and the reward is something she will give.

title: Pizza Coupon
text: Tony's Pizza: Student Special! Buy any large pizza and get a medium pizza free. Show your student ID when you order. Valid Sunday to Thursday only. Not valid with other offers. Offer ends May 31. Delivery costs $2 extra.

stem: When can a student use this offer?
options: On any day of the week
explanation: The coupon says it is 'Valid Sunday to Thursday only.' Friday and Saturday are not included.

stem: What must a student do to get the free pizza?
explanation: The offer is 'Buy any large pizza and get a medium pizza free.' Delivery costs extra but is not required, and the coupon cannot be used with other offers.

title: Club Fair Volunteers
text:
Subject: Club Fair help
Hello Kwame, thank you for joining the Hiking Club! We need three volunteers to help at our table at the Club Fair on September 12 from 10 a.m. to noon. You would show photos from our trips and give out flyers. Please reply by Friday if you can come. Olga, Club President

stem: What does Olga ask Kwame to do?
options: Reply if he can help at the fair
explanation: Olga writes 'Please reply by Friday if you can come,' so she wants to know whether he can help at the table. He is not asked to take photos; photos from earlier trips will be shown.

stem: What would the volunteers do at the table?
options: Show pictures and hand out flyers
explanation: The email says volunteers 'would show photos from our trips and give out flyers.' It does not mention selling tickets or collecting money.

title: Office Hours Change
text:
Subject: Office hours this week
Dear students, I have to attend a conference on Wednesday, so my usual office hours are cancelled. Instead, I will be available on Thursday from 2 to 4 p.m. If you want feedback on your essay drafts before the deadline, please email them to me by Tuesday night, and I will reply with comments on Wednesday morning. Professor Nasser

stem: What is the main purpose of the email?
options: To announce a new deadline for the essay drafts
To explain how to write comments on drafts
To invite students to a conference on Wednesday
To explain a change in office hours
explanation: Professor Nasser says his 'usual office hours are cancelled' and offers a different time, so the email explains a change in office hours. The deadline is mentioned but not changed, and the conference is the reason, not an invitation.

stem: How can a student get feedback on a draft before the deadline?
options: Come to class on Thursday morning
Email the draft by Tuesday night
explanation: The professor asks students to 'email them to me by Tuesday night' and promises comments on Wednesday morning. Visiting on Wednesday is tempting, but his office hours that day are cancelled.

title: Covering a Shift
text:
Dina (1:15): Can you cover my shift at the library desk on Friday? I have a dentist appointment.
Omar (1:20): What time is it? I have lab until 3.
Dina (1:21): 4 to 8.
Omar (1:25): I could do 5 to 8 if someone else takes the first hour.
Dina (1:26): Perfect, I'll ask Jess about 4 to 5. I owe you one!

stem: What problem does Dina have?
options: She cannot work her scheduled shift
She has a lab report due at three
She forgot the time of her shift
She wants to move her dentist visit
explanation: Dina asks Omar to 'cover my shift' because she has a dentist appointment, so she cannot work it herself. The lab until 3 is Omar's schedule, not hers.

stem: What does Dina mean when she says, 'I owe you one!'?
options: She will pay Omar for the extra hours
She is sorry she did not ask earlier in the week
She is thankful and will return the favor
She wants him to take one more shift
explanation: 'I owe you one' is an informal way to say she is thankful and will do a favor for him later. It is not about money, and she does not ask for another shift.

title: Scholarship Deadline
text: Applications for the Global Learners Scholarship are due by March 15. Applicants must have a grade average of at least 3.0 and write a 300-word essay about their goals. Two teacher letters are also required. Late forms will not be considered, so please submit everything online before midnight on the due date.

stem: According to the notice, what must all applicants provide?
options: A report on their last semester
A short essay on future plans
explanation: The notice requires 'a 300-word essay about their goals,' which is a short essay on future plans. Volunteer work, jobs and semester reports are never mentioned.

stem: What does the phrase 'will not be considered' mean in the notice?
options: will be reviewed after a delay
will be sent back for corrections
explanation: 'Will not be considered' means the committee will not look at late forms at all. The notice does not describe any delayed review, corrections or lower scores.

title: Free Trial Ending
text: Your free trial of StudyBox ends in 2 days. After that, your card will be charged $4.99 each month unless you cancel. Your saved notes and flashcards will stay in your account. To stop the charge, go to Settings, then Subscription, and tap Cancel before Friday.

stem: What will happen if the user does nothing?
options: The account will be deleted on Friday
The user will be charged every month
The saved notes will be lost
The trial will continue for free
explanation: The message says 'your card will be charged $4.99 each month unless you cancel.' The notes stay in the account, so they will not be lost.

stem: What should a user do to avoid paying?
options: Remove the saved notes from the app
Wait until the free trial period ends
Change the card used for the account
Cancel the subscription in the app
explanation: The message explains: 'go to Settings, then Subscription, and tap Cancel before Friday.' Waiting for the trial to end is wrong because the charge starts then.

title: Room for Rent
text: Room for rent! I am going abroad for a semester and need someone to take my room from January to May. It is a quiet two-bedroom apartment, ten minutes' walk from campus. Rent is $400 a month, and internet is included. My roommate is friendly and works nights. Message me if interested. No smoking, please.

stem: Why is the writer posting this message?
options: To sell furniture before moving abroad
To look for a permanent roommate
To advertise a new apartment building
explanation: The writer will be abroad 'from January to May' and needs 'someone to take my room' for that time, so the writer wants a temporary tenant. The writer will return, so a permanent roommate is not wanted.

stem: What can be inferred about the roommate?
options: The roommate is moving abroad as well
The roommate will pay part of the internet cost
The roommate is often out in the evenings
The roommate prefers a noisy home
explanation: The roommate 'works nights,' so the roommate is probably away in the evenings. The apartment is described as quiet, and internet is already included in the rent.

title: Heating Inspection
text:
Subject: Maintenance visit
Dear tenants, a technician will inspect the heating system in all apartments on Monday between 9 a.m. and 3 p.m. You do not need to be home, but please make sure pets are secured and that the technician can reach the radiators. If you prefer to be present, call the office to arrange a specific time. Building Manager

stem: What are tenants asked to do before the visit?
options: Stay home all day on Monday
Make sure the radiators can be reached
Move their pets out of the building
Call the office to cancel the visit
explanation: The manager asks tenants to 'make sure pets are secured and that the technician can reach the radiators.' Staying home is optional, and calling the office is only for tenants who want to be present.

stem: What can be inferred about the inspection?
options: Every tenant must be at home for the inspection to happen
Only the apartments that have pets will be inspected
The technician will return to every apartment on Tuesday
The technician may enter when no one is at home
explanation: The manager says 'You do not need to be home,' which suggests the technician can enter an empty apartment. The inspection covers 'all apartments,' not only those with pets.

title: Movie Plans
text:
Mateo (7:30): Want to see the new movie tonight? It starts at 9.
Lena (7:32): I'd love to, but I'm swamped. I have a presentation tomorrow morning.
Mateo (7:33): No worries. How about Saturday instead?
Lena (7:35): Saturday works. Let's do the early show, though. I'm not a night owl.
Mateo (7:36): Deal. I'll buy the tickets for the 4:30 one.

stem: What does Lena mean when she says she is 'swamped'?
options: She is waiting a long time for a ride
She is feeling sick at home
She has a great deal of work
She does not like the movie
explanation: Lena explains right after: 'I have a presentation tomorrow morning.' 'Swamped' means having too much to do. She says she would love to go, so she does not dislike the film.

stem: What will Mateo probably do next?
options: Invite Lena to a different film
Buy tickets for Saturday's early show
Go to the movie tonight by himself
explanation: Mateo says 'I'll buy the tickets for the 4:30 one,' and Lena prefers the early show on Saturday. He accepts her suggestion rather than going alone.

title: Course Waitlist
text: If a course is full, you may join the waitlist through the student portal. Waitlisted students are not guaranteed a place. If a seat opens, the system will email you, and you will have 24 hours to accept it. After that, the seat goes to the next student. Please attend the first class meeting even if you are on the waitlist.

stem: What is the main purpose of the notice?
options: To explain how a course waitlist works
To announce that a course is cancelled
To ask students to drop a course
To list the new courses this term
explanation: The notice describes how to join the waitlist, what happens when a seat opens and the 24-hour limit, so it explains how the waitlist works.

stem: What happens if a student does not reply to the email within 24 hours?
options: The student is removed from the university
The student receives a second email
The course is closed to everyone
The place is offered to someone else
explanation: The notice says 'After that, the seat goes to the next student.' It does not mention a second email or any penalty.

title: Green Plate Specials
text:
Green Plate Kitchen: Today's Specials
Mushroom soup (contains milk): $5
Grilled fish with rice and beans: $9
Peanut noodle bowl (contains peanuts): $8
Fruit cup: $3
If you have a food allergy, please tell your server before ordering. We cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free of nuts.

stem: Which special should a person with a milk allergy avoid?
explanation: Only the mushroom soup is marked '(contains milk).' The noodle bowl is marked for peanuts, which is a different allergy.

stem: What can be inferred from the last sentence of the menu?
options: Every dish on the menu contains nuts
Servers cannot answer questions about food
A dish may touch nuts even if none are listed
explanation: The restaurant 'cannot guarantee that any dish is completely free of nuts,' so even a dish without listed nuts might have been in contact with them. It does not say all dishes contain nuts.

title: Saturday Express Train
text:
Express Train to Riverton: Saturday
Departs City Station: 8:10, 10:10, 12:10, 2:10
Arrives Riverton: 9:25, 11:25, 1:25, 3:25
Seats cannot be reserved. Please arrive 15 minutes early, as the train fills quickly on weekends. Bicycles are allowed on the 8:10 and 10:10 trains only.

stem: A passenger with a bicycle needs to arrive in Riverton after 10:00 a.m. but before noon. Which train should the passenger take?
explanation: The 10:10 train arrives at 11:25 and allows bicycles. The 8:10 train arrives at 9:25, which is too early, and the later trains do not allow bicycles.

stem: Why does the timetable advise passengers to arrive 15 minutes early?
options: People who come late may not get a seat
The train often leaves ahead of schedule
Tickets are checked at the gate
explanation: Seats 'cannot be reserved' and the train 'fills quickly on weekends,' so late passengers may find no seat. The text never says the train leaves early.

title: Student Parking Rules
text:
STUDENT PARKING RULES
Permits are required in Lots A and C from Monday to Friday. After 6 p.m., Lot C is for residents only. Cars parked in fire lanes will be towed immediately. Overnight parking is not allowed, except in Lot A with a green permit. Parking is free on weekends in all lots.

stem: According to the rules, where can a car stay overnight?
options: In Lot C, for residents only
In any lot, if it is the weekend
In Lot A, with a green permit
In a fire lane, with a permit
explanation: The rules say 'Overnight parking is not allowed, except in Lot A with a green permit.' Lot C is for residents after 6 p.m. but that does not allow overnight parking, and weekend parking is free, not overnight.

stem: What does the word 'immediately' suggest about parking in a fire lane?
options: Drivers will get a warning first
Drivers get no time to move the car
The fee is paid on the spot
explanation: 'Towed immediately' means the car is taken away at once, without a chance to move it. A warning or a payment on the spot is not mentioned.

title: Outdoor Store Order
text:
Order #4821: Thank you for shopping at Northside Outfitters.
1 pair hiking boots (size 9): $82.00
1 rain jacket (medium): $59.00
Shipping: free for orders over $100
Estimated delivery: 5 to 7 business days.
Unworn items can be exchanged for a different size within 30 days.

stem: Why is the shipping free for this order?
options: The order is above a set amount
explanation: The boots and jacket cost $141 together, and shipping is 'free for orders over $100.' The receipt mentions no student discount, sale or gift.

stem: What can the customer do if the boots do not fit?
options: Return them for cash at any time
Keep them and receive a discount
Ask for a refund after seven days
Exchange them if they are unworn
explanation: The receipt says 'Unworn items can be exchanged for a different size within 30 days.' A cash refund is not offered, and the exchange time limit is 30 days.

title: Pasta Night
text: Cooking Club Pop-up! Join us Friday at 6 p.m. in the Dorm B kitchen to learn how to make fresh pasta from scratch. We have space for twelve people, and spots are first come, first served. Sign up on the board outside the kitchen. All ingredients are provided, but bring an apron if you have one!

stem: What does 'first come, first served' mean in the post?
options: Food is served before the class
Guests may arrive at any time
explanation: Because there are only twelve spots, 'first come, first served' means the people who sign up first get the places. It is not about the order of food or about arrival times.

stem: What should a person do to join the pop-up?
options: Send an email to the club
Add a name to the list by the kitchen
Bring the ingredients for the pasta
Pay a small fee at the door
explanation: The post says 'Sign up on the board outside the kitchen.' The club provides the ingredients, and no fee is mentioned.

title: Internship Interview
text:
Subject: Interview confirmation
Dear Ms. Okafor, thank you for applying for the summer internship. We would like to invite you to an interview on Tuesday, June 4, at 10:30 a.m. at our downtown office, Suite 210. Please bring a copy of your resume and a photo ID for building security. If the time is not convenient, let us know by Friday and we will try to find another slot. Daniel Brooks, HR

stem: What is the main purpose of the email?
options: To offer Ms. Okafor an internship
To ask for a copy of her resume
To say her application was not accepted
To invite her to an interview
explanation: Mr. Brooks writes 'We would like to invite you to an interview.' He asks for a resume to be brought, but that is a detail, and no job offer or rejection is given.

stem: What should Ms. Okafor do if the interview time does not suit her?
options: Send her photo ID by email
Wait for a call on Tuesday
explanation: The email says 'let us know by Friday and we will try to find another slot.' Photo ID is for building security on the day of the interview.

title: Library Quiet Zones
text: Quiet Zones: The third floor of the library is a silent study area. Phone calls and group talks are not permitted there. Students who wish to work together should use the group rooms on the first floor, which can be booked at the front desk for up to two hours. Please set your phone to silent mode on all floors.

stem: Where should students go to work on a group project?
options: The silent area on the third floor
Any floor, if they speak softly
The rooms that can be reserved
explanation: The notice says students who want to work together 'should use the group rooms on the first floor, which can be booked.' The third floor is for silent study.

stem: What does the notice say about phones?
options: They are banned on the third floor
They may be used for calls in group rooms
They should be on silent on every floor
They must be left at the front desk
explanation: The last sentence asks students to 'set your phone to silent mode on all floors.' Phone calls are not permitted in the silent area, but the phones themselves are not banned or collected.

title: Package Alert
text: Package Alert: Your package from BookNest was left at the Mailroom because no one answered the door. Pick it up between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m., Monday to Friday, and bring your student ID. Packages are held for 7 days, after which they are sent back to the sender.

stem: Where is the package now?
explanation: The alert says the package 'was left at the Mailroom because no one answered the door.' It is not at the door or in the room.

stem: What will probably happen if the student waits ten days to collect the package?
options: The student must pay a late fee
It may be returned to the sender
The mailroom will deliver it again
The student ID will be cancelled
explanation: Packages are 'held for 7 days, after which they are sent back to the sender.' Ten days is longer than that. No fee or second delivery is mentioned.

title: Chart Problem
text:
Ravi (4:05): Did you finish your part of the slides?
Mei (4:10): Almost. I'm stuck on the chart. The numbers don't add up.
Ravi (4:11): Send it over. I'll take a look.
Mei (4:15): It's the one on slide 6.
Ravi (4:30): Found it. You were counting the last year twice. Fixed.
Mei (4:32): You're a lifesaver!

stem: What was wrong with the chart?
options: The numbers were typed too small
Some data was counted two times
The chart was on the wrong slide
explanation: Ravi says 'You were counting the last year twice,' which means the same data appeared two times. This is why the numbers did not add up.

stem: What does Mei mean when she says, 'You're a lifesaver!'?
options: He saved the file before it was lost
He is the best student in the class
He should finish the whole project
She is very grateful for his help
explanation: 'Lifesaver' is used to thank someone who helped in a difficult moment. Mei is grateful that Ravi solved her chart problem. It is not about saving a file.

title: Spring Music Night
text:
SPRING MUSIC NIGHT
A concert by the University Orchestra and Jazz Band. Saturday, April 12, 7 p.m., Greenfield Hall. Doors open at 6:30. Entry is free for students with ID. Guests pay $5 at the door. Seating is open, so come early for the best seats. No food or drink in the hall.

stem: Who must pay $5 at the door?
explanation: Entry is 'free for students with ID' and 'Guests pay $5 at the door.' So people who are not students pay. Arrival time does not affect the price.

stem: Why does the flyer suggest coming early?
options: Food is sold before the show
The ID check takes an hour
Places are not reserved in advance
explanation: 'Seating is open, so come early for the best seats' means seats are not assigned ahead of time, and early arrivals choose first. The doors open at 6:30, but the hall does not close then.

title: Guest Policy Reminder
text:
Subject: Guest policy reminder
Dear residents, overnight guests are welcome for up to three nights a month, but you must register them at the front desk before 10 p.m. Guests need a photo ID. You are responsible for your guest's behavior. If a guest breaks the rules, you may lose guest privileges for the semester. Residence Life

stem: What is the main purpose of the email?
options: To announce a new fee for visitors
To review the rules for guests
To ask guests to leave early
explanation: The email lists the limit on nights, the registration time and the ID requirement, so it reviews the rules for overnight guests. No fee is announced.

stem: What can be inferred about a resident whose guest breaks the rules?
options: The resident will move to another dorm
The guest will have to pay a fine
The resident could lose a privilege
explanation: The email says 'You are responsible for your guest's behavior' and the resident 'may lose guest privileges for the semester.' So the resident can be affected by the guest's actions.

title: Orientation Day
text:
New Student Orientation: Friday
9:00 Welcome speech, Main Hall
10:00 Campus tour (Groups A and B) or library workshop (Groups C and D)
11:30 Lunch, cafeteria
12:30 Campus tour (Groups C and D) or library workshop (Groups A and B)
2:00 Meet your advisor
Bring your student card to get your lunch voucher.

stem: A student in Group C goes to the 10:00 session. What will she do?
explanation: The 10:00 line gives the library workshop to Groups C and D, so a Group C student attends it. The campus tour for her group is at 12:30.

stem: When do Groups A and B attend the library workshop?
explanation: The 12:30 line says Groups A and B have the library workshop then; they take the tour at 10:00. Lunch is at 11:30 for everyone.

title: Free Bike Repair
text: Free Bike Repair! Come to the Student Center plaza on Wednesday from 12 to 2 p.m. A mechanic will fix flat tires and loose chains. You do not need to pay, but you must bring your own bike. If it rains, the event will move to the garage next door.

stem: Where will the event be if it rains?
explanation: The notice says 'If it rains, the event will move to the garage next door.' The plaza is the place for dry weather.

stem: What must people bring to the event?
explanation: The notice says 'you must bring your own bike.' The repair is free, so no money is needed.

title: Waiting Outside
text:
Ana (5:10): I'm outside the dorm. Where are you?
Tariq (5:11): Sorry! I'm still at the gym. I'll be there in ten minutes.
Ana (5:12): OK. I'll wait in the cafe next door.
Tariq (5:13): Great. Can you order me a tea, please?
Ana (5:14): Sure.

stem: Where is Tariq now?
explanation: Tariq writes, 'I'm still at the gym.' Ana is the one outside the dorm, and she will wait in the cafe.

stem: What does Tariq ask Ana to do?
explanation: Tariq asks, 'Can you order me a tea, please?' So he wants her to buy him a drink.

title: Breakfast Menu
text:
Sunrise Cafe: Breakfast
Pancakes with fruit: $5
Eggs on toast: $4
Oatmeal with honey: $3
Served from 7 to 10:30 a.m. Coffee or tea is $1 extra. Ask about our gluten-free bread.

stem: Which breakfast costs the least?
explanation: Oatmeal with honey costs $3, which is less than $4 for eggs and $5 for pancakes. Coffee or tea is an extra $1 and is not a breakfast.

stem: Until what time is breakfast served?
explanation: The menu says breakfast is 'Served from 7 to 10:30 a.m.' so it ends at 10:30. Seven o'clock is the starting time.

title: Quiz on Monday
text:
Subject: Quiz on Monday
Hello class, there will be a short quiz on Chapters 3 and 4 on Monday. It will take 15 minutes at the start of class. You may use a pencil or a pen. Calculators are not allowed. Please come on time. Dr. Silva

stem: What is the email about?
explanation: Dr. Silva writes 'there will be a short quiz on Chapters 3 and 4 on Monday.' A quiz is a short test.

stem: What is not allowed during the quiz?
explanation: The email says 'Calculators are not allowed.' Students may use a pencil or a pen.

title: Recycling Reminder
text: Recycling Reminder: Please rinse bottles and cans before putting them in the blue bins. Paper goes in the green bins, but greasy pizza boxes must go in the regular trash because the oil spoils the paper. Bins are emptied on Tuesdays and Fridays. Thank you for keeping our campus clean.

stem: What should a person do with a greasy pizza box?
options: Throw it away with regular trash
Rinse it and put it in a blue bin
Put it in the green bin with paper
Leave it next to the bins for staff
explanation: The notice says 'greasy pizza boxes must go in the regular trash.' Paper goes in the green bins, but the oil makes this box unsuitable.

stem: The word 'spoils' in the notice is closest in meaning to
explanation: 'The oil spoils the paper' means the oil ruins it so it cannot be recycled. The other words do not describe a harmful effect.

title: Debate Club Room Change
text:
Subject: Change of room
Hi all, tonight's Debate Club meeting has been moved from Room 110 to Room 305 because the projector in 110 is broken. We will start at the same time, 6 p.m. If you are already on your way to 110, please check the sign on the door. I will leave directions there. Bring your topic cards. Hamza

stem: Why was the meeting moved?
options: Too many members plan to attend
The earlier room is too small
The projector there does not work
explanation: Hamza says it was moved 'because the projector in 110 is broken.' The time stays the same, and nothing is said about crowding or cleaning.

stem: What should a member do who goes to Room 110 by mistake?
options: Read the sign on the door
explanation: Hamza writes 'please check the sign on the door. I will leave directions there.' Waiting in the wrong room would not help.

title: Book Buyback Week
text: Book Buyback Week! Sell your used textbooks back to the Campus Bookstore from December 10 to 14. Prices depend on the condition of the book and on whether it will be used next semester. Books with highlighting are accepted, but books with torn covers are not. Bring a photo ID. Cash is paid on the spot.

stem: What affects the price offered for a book?
options: Whether the school will use it again
explanation: The post says prices depend on condition 'and on whether it will be used next semester.' This means whether the school will use it again.

stem: What can be inferred about a textbook with a torn cover?
options: The store will not buy it
It can be sold on the last day only
explanation: The post says books with torn covers 'are not' accepted, so the store will not buy them. Highlighted books are accepted, so highlighting is not the problem.

title: Lost in Economics
text:
Jess (8:20): Did you understand the lecture on supply and demand? I'm totally lost.
Kofi (8:24): Honestly, I'm in the same boat. The graphs confused me.
Jess (8:25): Maybe we should go to the tutoring center?
Kofi (8:27): Good idea. They open at 10. Meet there?
Jess (8:28): See you at 9:55. I'll get us coffee first.

stem: What does Kofi mean when he says, 'I'm in the same boat'?
options: He wants to leave the class
explanation: Kofi answers Jess's problem with 'The graphs confused me,' so he also has trouble understanding the lecture. The idiom means being in the same situation.

stem: What will Jess probably do before the tutoring center opens?
explanation: Jess says 'I'll get us coffee first.' She plans to meet Kofi at 9:55, just before the center opens at 10.

title: Refund Policy
text: Please be advised that the Bursar's Office will process refunds for dropped courses only if the withdrawal is filed prior to the end of the second week of classes. Requests submitted thereafter will be assessed on a case-by-case basis and are contingent upon documented extenuating circumstances.

stem: What can be inferred about a student who drops a course in the fourth week?
options: The student will automatically get a full refund
The student will be prevented from leaving the course
The student will have to pay a penalty fee
The student might not get any money back
explanation: After the second week, requests are judged 'case-by-case' and need documented circumstances, so a refund is not guaranteed. The notice does not mention a penalty or a ban on dropping.

stem: The phrase 'contingent upon' is closest in meaning to
explanation: 'Contingent upon documented extenuating circumstances' means the decision depends on whether the student can document special reasons. 'Dependent on' expresses that relationship.

title: Following Up
text:
Subject: Following up
Hi Dr. Moreau, I hope your week is going well. I wanted to touch base about the recommendation letter we discussed in October. The scholarship portal closes on the 20th, and I understand how busy this period must be. If it would be easier, I am happy to send a summary of my projects to jog your memory. With thanks, Imani

stem: Why does Imani write to Dr. Moreau?
options: To politely check on a promised letter
To apologize for missing a deadline
To ask for a summary of a class
explanation: Imani wants to 'touch base' about a letter they discussed and mentions the closing date, so she is gently reminding the professor. She does not apologize or cancel anything.

stem: Why does Imani offer to send a summary of her projects?
options: To prove she deserves the scholarship
To make the professor's task easier
To change the topic of the letter
explanation: She offers it 'to jog your memory' and 'if it would be easier,' which shows she wants to help the professor write the letter. The summary supports the letter, not replaces it.

title: River Cleanup Thanks
text: Thanks to everyone who showed up to Saturday's cleanup! We expected a handful of volunteers and ended up with nearly sixty. The riverbank hasn't looked this good in years, though the north stretch still needs attention. We're hoping to tackle it next month, provided the weather cooperates. Keep an eye on this page for the date. Riverside Neighbors Group

stem: What can be inferred about the turnout at the cleanup?
options: It was close to what the organizers expected
It was lower than at last year's event
It was far higher than the group planned
It was disappointing to the volunteers
explanation: The group 'expected a handful of volunteers and ended up with nearly sixty,' so far more people came than planned. The tone of the thanks shows the organizers were pleased.

stem: What does the group mean by 'provided the weather cooperates'?
options: The date was chosen from the forecast
The next cleanup depends on good weather
explanation: 'Provided' means 'if,' so the cleanup will happen only if the weather allows. The group has not yet announced a date, so the date was not chosen from a forecast.

title: Late Work FAQ
text: Quick answers about late work: Instructors set their own policies, and most accept late papers with a grade reduction of five percent per day. However, lab reports are rarely accepted late, since results are discussed in class the following week. If illness or an emergency prevents you from submitting on time, contact your instructor before the deadline whenever possible.

stem: According to the page, why are lab reports rarely accepted late?
options: Results are reviewed in class soon after
They lose five percent each day
Students rarely finish them on time
explanation: The page explains that 'results are discussed in class the following week,' so a late report would come after the discussion. The five percent reduction applies to late papers in general.

stem: What does the page advise a student who may miss a deadline because of illness?
options: Tell the instructor in advance if possible
Submit the work without a grade
Wait until the grade reduction applies
Ask the lab for new results
explanation: The page says to 'contact your instructor before the deadline whenever possible.' Waiting would only add a penalty, and no other action is suggested.
